transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the pre-publication check-in for our catalog. I'd like to focus on 'Glass Harbor' — the current draft lists it at 94 minutes with premiere status still marked for confirmation. Before I make a final programming decision on whether it goes into the national competition or the panorama program, I need our submissions and technical screening staff to report any status or master-file issues they're aware of. Can someone from submissions speak to the premiere status, and can technical screening confirm the runtime and whether we have an approved screening master on file?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the national festival database yesterday and confirmed that 'Glass Harbor' already had a public screening at the Coastline Film Week in this country. I recorded the result in my local review notes, but the database export feeding your catalog review has not yet refreshed, which is likely why the premiere status is still marked for confirmation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good morning, Mara. I completed ingest quality control this morning and confirmed that the filmmaker's approved festival cut is an 88-minute DCP, not the 94 minutes listed in the catalog draft. The QC report is currently waiting in the technical queue and has not yet been attached to the programming record, which is likely why the catalog still shows the older runtime. So to directly answer your questions: the approved screening master on file is an 88-minute DCP, and we do have it in our system.
transcript.speaker: A3
